episode_title: PMs Are Dead... but Nobody Decided That | AA276

real_qa.q: What does the 2026 CPO Insights report claim about product manager headcount decline and future role elimination?
real_qa.r: According to the 2026 CPO Insights report from Products That Count, traditional product manager headcount has declined by as much as 30 percent overall, with a 70 percent decline in SaaS. The report makes a bold prediction that by 2030 the role of product manager will cease to exist and will be replaced by the product builder role.
real_qa.requete: 2026 CPO Insights report product manager headcount decline

real_qa.q: What does the CPO Insights report say is replacing traditional product managers?
real_qa.r: The report states that product builders will replace traditional product managers. Product builders discover, prototype, build and deploy with AI velocity, with the goal to deliver 2x better value at 10x speed. Product builders are increasing at a 10x pace and are described as high leverage operators capable of rapidly testing bets, iterating on signals, and scaling what works.
real_qa.requete: product builders replacing product managers 2026 report

real_qa.q: How does the TrueUp data show the relationship between the 2022 PM hiring peak and current job market trends?
real_qa.r: The host notes that 2022 represented an artificial peak in hiring when Silicon Valley was over-hiring to keep competitors from hiring talented people. This was during a labor market rather than an employer market. The decline from that 2022 peak does not necessarily indicate a structural decline in the PM role, but rather a correction from abnormal over-hiring combined with broader tech market contraction that affected all tech roles equally.
real_qa.requete: TrueUp product manager jobs 2022 peak decline

real_qa.q: What statistical issues does the host identify with how the 30 percent PM headcount decline figure is presented?
real_qa.r: The host observes that the report uses inconsistent verb tenses throughout, that the 30 percent number appears to be rounded from a more precise 28 percent figure from another source, and that the comparison measures from a 2022 hiring spike rather than a longer-term average. The host argues this represents either bad faith cherry-picking or sloppiness in reporting, and notes that the same general decline appears across all tech roles, not just PM positions.
real_qa.requete: CPO Insights report statistics methodology problems 30 percent

real_qa.q: According to Marty Cagan, what is the core bottleneck in product management?
real_qa.r: Marty Cagan, speaking on the Modern CTO podcast in June 2026, stated that the bottleneck is now much more appropriately recognized as figuring out what you want these people to build, and that is the product management role in a nutshell. He defines product management as figuring out something worth building.
real_qa.requete: Marty Cagan product management bottleneck worth building
